note: Gives a structured way to say which claims a given benchmark can support, which is the core judgement in reviewing a vendor evidence.
title: Measurement to Meaning: A Validity-Centered Framework for AI Evaluation
explain_beginner: The paper offers a way to judge what an AI test score really proves. It notes that AI systems have improved quickly, but common evaluation practices have not kept up. A strong result on one narrow test, such as advanced exam questions, is often used to support a much bigger claim, such as broad reasoning ability. That leap can mislead. The framework asks whether the evidence actually supports the specific claim being made. For example, a math score may only show performance on that kind of math task, not wider thinking. This matters because people who rely on AI claims need clearer grounds for trusting them.
explain_business: For executives, this paper is a warning about AI evidence. A vendor may claim broad capability, but the supporting test may only cover a narrow task. The framework helps you ask whether the evidence actually supports the exact claim you care about. It gives a structured way to review benchmarks and decide if they justify adoption, procurement, or deployment. It also helps teams request evaluations that match business needs. The practical decision is whether to trust a vendor's claim, ask for stronger proof, or limit use to the scope the evidence supports. This reduces risk from overbroad AI promises.
explain_practitioner: The paper proposes a validity focused framework for AI evaluation. It uses ideas from psychometrics to break validity into parts, then asks which parts matter for a given claim. This helps researchers decide whether a benchmark result supports a narrow skill or a broader ability. The framework also guides evaluation design by showing which evidence is most important for the intended claim. The authors apply it to vision and language model examples. The key result is that making validity explicit makes the tie between test results and stated claims clearer, which can improve practical usefulness and decision quality.
